evidence.text: The exact file page identifies 天-seal.svg as a modern vector depiction of 天 in Shuowen seal-script style. It names a Xiaoxuetang image (27.5929) as a source for this picture and links the original SVG at https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/2/26/%E5%A4%A9-seal.svg. The page states CC0 1.0. This is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

evidence.source: 漢字構形資料庫, Academia Sinica
evidence.field: 字形演變; oracle-bone and bronze form records; editorial explanation
evidence.text: The page lists oracle-bone example 合集19050 and bronze example 集成02836. Its interpretation describes 天 as a frontal standing human with an emphasized head, later reduced to a horizontal stroke, and proposes extension from the head to the sky above. This is the database’s analysis, not an independently dated reading of each inscription.

gaps: The direct SVG could not be rendered by the web tool, so its visible strokes were not independently inspected in this research. The identity, source attribution, period label, and reuse notice come from its exact Commons description page.

The Shuowen seal-script image is a modern vector redraw, not a dated artifact image. Its selection illustrates a later script form, while the human-figure/head account is based on paleographic interpretations of earlier forms; the seal redraw alone cannot establish that interpretation or semantic chronology.

The inspected Academia Sinica account supports the wording that 大 is the graphic basis for the person and the upper mark emphasizes the head. It proposes a head-to-sky extension, but the dossier also records a competing sky-first analysis; the earliest spoken sense and semantic sequence remain unresolved.

items.period: Shuowen seal-script style; modern digital redraw of a historical script form
items.caption: A modern redraw of 天 in Shuowen seal-script style. The earlier head-marked human-figure interpretation is supported by paleographic accounts, but this later form alone does not establish whether “head/top” or “sky” was the earliest spoken meaning.
items.alt: Modern vector rendering of the character 天 in a seal-script style, as identified by the Commons file page; pixels not independently inspected in this research.
items.selection_reason: The failed oracle-script file is replaced with this separately verified, reusable Tian form. It provides an attested later script tradition relevant to the graph's history; its caption avoids treating the redraw as an ancient artifact or as proof of a disputed semantic sequence.
items.rights: The Commons description page states CC0 1.0 and attributes a source image to Academia Sinica Xiaoxuetang; the page also notes a Richard Sears source agreement for other material. The selected file's page explicitly makes this vector available under CC0 1.0.

limitations.text: The image is a modern vector redraw of a Shuowen seal-script form, not a photograph of a dated inscription. The direct SVG could not be rendered by the web tool; its provenance and rights were verified from the exact Commons description page, but its pixels were not independently inspected.
The head-marked analysis and the competing sky-first account do not establish one certain earliest spoken sense or a complete head/top-to-sky semantic chronology.
